decisions.question: When should a future fresh inventory be proposed for portable CPU admission work?

options.label: Just-in-time digest-bound refresh
options.effect: Preserve R1 as immutable evidence after expiry and prepare a new one-attempt refresh package only after compatibility, workload, policy, and candidate records are sealed, so inventory can be fresh at admission review.
options.tradeoff: Best freshness and least unnecessary machine access; later progress waits for another explicit owner authorization.

options.label: Refresh at each planning milestone
options.effect: Request a separate one-time inventory authorization after each major planning package.
options.tradeoff: More current snapshots but repeated owner actions and rapidly stale evidence before admission is otherwise ready.

options.label: Reusable periodic collector
options.effect: Design a product collector and schedule recurring refreshes.
options.tradeoff: Operationally convenient but materially expands implementation, security, privacy, and machine-access scope; not authorized now.

options.label: Waive or extend expiry
options.effect: Treat R1 as admission-fresh beyond the accepted 24-hour validity window.
options.tradeoff: Conflicts with the accepted fail-closed A/A/A/A policy and is not recommended.

decisions.question: What evidence must exist before portable_cpu can enter the resolver candidate set?

options.label: Strict seven-input fail-closed admission
options.effect: Require fresh inventory, authorization, policy, compatibility, workload, pipeline, and capacity inputs plus generated validation before candidate eligibility; an unknown or stale input rejects the candidate.
options.tradeoff: Strongest deterministic and auditable behavior; requires completing every evidence record.

options.label: Inventory-only provisional eligibility
options.effect: Allow portable_cpu into the candidate set from inventory and planning policy alone while other inputs remain pending.
options.tradeoff: Speeds UI and resolver demonstrations but weakens the shared fail-closed contract and risks accidental execution paths.

options.label: Manual operator activation
options.effect: Permit an operator override to activate portable_cpu despite missing compatibility or capacity evidence.
options.tradeoff: Bypasses hard gates that operator controls are explicitly prohibited from waiving.

options.label: Defer portable CPU profile
options.effect: Keep the profile entirely outside future resolver planning until accelerated or server profiles are available.
options.tradeoff: Reduces near-term work but removes the laptop and CI reference path.

decisions.question: What must the portable CPU compatibility bundle contain before validation?

options.label: Complete immutable compatibility bundle
options.effect: Bind exact model, runtime, provider, precision, artifacts, provenance, SBOM, signature, vulnerability report, pipeline digests, license, security expiry, fallback, rollback, profile target, and policy references.
options.tradeoff: Largest planning package but supports deterministic replay, supply-chain review, promotion, rollback, and future server portability.

options.label: Model and runtime bundle only
options.effect: Bind model, runtime, provider, precision, and dependency hashes without complete pipeline, security, fallback, or rollback records.
options.tradeoff: Smaller package but remains ineligible under the shared compatibility schema and cannot support safe promotion.

options.label: Mutable local environment reference
options.effect: Use the current lockfile and local environment state instead of a content-addressed compatibility snapshot.
options.tradeoff: Easy locally but non-reproducible across collaborator laptops and future Government servers.

options.label: No compatibility bundle
options.effect: Rely on runtime auto-detection and fallback.
options.tradeoff: Contradicts the accepted immutable-bundle and no-silent-fallback decisions.

decisions.question: What non-executable validation design should be sealed before any later generated-only runtime authorization?

options.label: Deterministic CONTRACT plus INFER matrix
options.effect: Predeclare generated-only CONTRACT and C1 INFER layers, fixed seeds, cold start, warm steady state, bounded burst, dependency loss, safe shutdown, warmup and measured iterations, repetitions, resource ceilings, recovery checks, and balanced/throughput/latency reports with balanced as default.
options.tradeoff: Most complete laptop-safe design and directly reusable for stronger hardware profiles; exact numeric values still require a later sealed proposal before execution.

options.label: Minimal deterministic smoke
options.effect: Validate one generated tensor, one inference, output contract, and shutdown only.
options.tradeoff: Fast but cannot establish batching, queue, resource, recovery, or objective-mode evidence.

options.label: Throughput stress first
options.effect: Prioritize sustained maximum-load execution and optimize throughput before parity and recovery evidence.
options.tradeoff: Resource aggressive, not authorized, unsuitable for the current laptop, and weak as a correctness baseline.

options.label: Defer generated validation
options.effect: Keep the portable proposal planning-only with no validation design.
options.tradeoff: Avoids near-term work but leaves P36-G2 unchanged and prevents a defensible execution proposal.
